 JUDGEMENT

At the initial stage the petitioner has filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming the compensation of Rs.7,00,000/- with interest on account of the injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicles Accident.
Later on by filing amendment application, amended petition was filed wherein petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs.35,00,000/-.

2. The case of the petitioner is as under:
That, on 07.03.2014 at about 9.15 p.m, the petitioner was riding Hero Honda motor cycle bearing 3 SCCH-24.
M.V.C.2038/2014 Reg.No.KA-50-H-663 from Doddaballapura towards Yellapura, slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road near Essar Petrol Bunk, D.B.Pura - Bangalore road,
Doddaballapur Taluk.
At that time the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.HR-38-P-5918 coming from Essar Petrol Bunk in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed the motor cycle.
Due to the impact, motor cycle fell down along with rider and pillion rider, the petitioner who was riding the motor cycle sustained severe grievous injuries.
3. It is alleged that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Apurva Mother and Child Hospital, Yelahanka Old town.

Due to the injuries and hospitalization the petitioner has undergone enormous pain, suffering and mental agony.

The petitioner has spent Rs.2,50,000/-
towards medicine and Rs.50,000/- towards incidental expenses.

The accident in question 4 SCCH-24.

4. It is alleged that, prior to the date of accident, he was hale and healthy and was working as Quality Controller in a Factory and was drawing salary of Rs.7,500/- per month.
Due to the grievous injuries, prolonged treatment, the petitioner could not attend to his work and lost income.

sentences.text: The 1st respondent is the insurer and 2nd respondent is the RC owner of the lorry, hence both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

The jurisdictional Doddaballapura Police have registered a case against the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.HR-38-P-5918 in their crime No.83/2014 U/s 279 and 337 of the IPC and the said case is pending trial.
5. After service of notice, the Respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel before the Tribunal and resisted the petition by filing objection statement.

In spite of the service of notice Respondent No.2 has 5 SCCH-24.
M.V.C.2038/2014 remained absent.
Hence, he has been placed as exparte.
6. The respondent No.1 has denied all the averments made in the claim petition and specifically denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the lorry bearing Reg.No.HR-38-P-5918.

The respondent No.1 further denied the date, place and time of the accident, age, avocation, income,
treatment taken as inpatient, amount spent towards hospitalization, injuries sustained and called upon the petitioner to prove the same with strict proof.
The respondent No.1 has contended that, the driver of the lorry was not possessing valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
The said vehicle being a commercial vehicle, same was not in possession of valid permit and fitness certificate to ply on road, the same amounts to violation of policy conditions.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.

It is further contended that, the lorry bearing Reg.No.HR-38-P- 5918 was not at all involved in the accident, petitioner in collusion with the police, lodged a false complaint against the driver of the lorry.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, arbitrary.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition with exemplary costs against the 1st respondent.
On the basis of the above pleadings and the rival contentions of both the parties, the following issues were framed:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident that occurred on 07.03.2014 at about 9.15 a.m, while petitioner was riding his motor Hero Honda motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50- H-663, near Essar Petrol Bunk, D.B.Pura- Bangalore road, Kasaba Hobli, D.B.Pura Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, due to rash and negligent driving of the lorry bearing Reg.No.HR-38-P-5918 by its driver ?

24. It is pertinent to note that, Ex.P.1, i.e. the copy of the First Information Report discloses that,
criminal case has been registered against the driver of the Lorry for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.

After investigation, the police have filed the 14 SCCH-24.

Ex.P.3 is copy of Panchanama on the scene of the occurrence.
Ex.P.5 i.e wound certificate discloses that, the petitioner has sustained injuries in the said accident.
The police documents i.e., Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7 are marked without any objections.
Thus, the contents of Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7 prima-facie establishes the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry.
The respondents have not made any attempt to examine the driver of the said lorry to show that, there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the said lorry.
The driver of the lorry is the best witness to say about the accident and negligence.
The respondent No.1 has contended that, the driver of the lorry was not having valid Driving Licence and the said lorry was not possessing FC to ply on the road at the time of accident.
In this regard, this respondent has not produced any materials.
In the absence of the rebuttal evidence, an adverse inference can be drawn against the respondents.

Under these circumstances, the evidence of P.W.1, coupled with the contents of the police documents, establishes that, the accident has caused solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.HR-38-P-5918.

At the initial stage the petitioner has filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming the compensation of Rs.7,00,000/- with interest on account of the injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicles Accident.
Due to the impact, motor cycle fell down along with rider and pillion rider, the petitioner who was riding the motor cycle sustained severe grievous injuries.
Due to the grievous injuries, prolonged treatment, the petitioner could not attend to his work and lost income.
The 1st respondent is the insurer and 2nd respondent is the RC owner of the lorry, hence both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The jurisdictional Doddaballapura Police have registered a case against the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.HR-38-P-5918 in their crime No.83/2014 U/s 279 and 337 of the IPC and the said case is pending trial.

It is further contended that, the lorry bearing Reg.No.HR-38-P- 5918 was not at all involved in the accident, petitioner in collusion with the police, lodged a false complaint against the driver of the lorry.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, arbitrary.
